## Objective
- The user wants to enhance the existing pixel-art creature-catching game with distinctive animal-inspired starter creatures, a starter-selection building, and more complete creature battles.

## Requirements
- Maintain the existing pixel-art style.
- Add an enterable building with a table displaying three capsule-like Poké Ball items, each containing a distinct animal-inspired creature with its own design and color.
- Interacting with each starter displays its name; the player may choose only one.
- Give each creature two attacks and make chosen creatures usable in fights against visually distinct wild creatures found in tall grass.

## Decisions
- The game is an original creature-catching adventure with original characters and assets, not Pokémon characters or assets.
- Earlier work implemented the game as “Wildbound” in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing playable game has keyboard and touch movement, a meadow, encounters, capture, and saving.
- Added a second battle attack button and attack-name labels in `index.html`.

### Active
- Implement the requested starter-selection building, three animal-inspired starter designs, one-starter-only selection and naming interaction.
- Add distinct animal-based wild creature visuals.
- Implement two creature-specific attacks and use the selected creature in combat.
- Verify desktop and mobile gameplay after changes.

- `(none)`

1. Inspect current `game.js` and `index.html`; finish the second attack button wiring and update the battle action layout for four actions.
2. Add starter-selection flow, enter/exit interior, table with three interactable capsules, and persist the selected starter.
3. Draw distinct pixel-art starter and wild creatures and wire their identities/attacks into combat.
4. Test game in browser at desktop and mobile sizes, including choosing a starter, battles, and persistence.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Canvas world rendering, movement, party, encounters, battle logic, and save state.
- `index.html`: Game UI, battle overlay, and newly added second attack button.
- `style.css`: Pixel-art game styling and responsive mobile layouts.

## Important Context
- Current battle HTML has `#attack-btn`, newly inserted `#attack-two-btn`, `#catch-btn`, and `#run-btn`; existing JavaScript only wires `#attack-btn`, `#catch-btn`, and `#run-btn`.

## Objective
- Complete Wildbound as a creature-catching game with three animal-inspired starters, a starter-selection lodge, and battles featuring two attacks per creature.
- Verify gameplay, save persistence, and desktop/mobile presentation.

## Requirements
- Preserve the existing pixel-art style and use original creatures and assets.
- Let players enter the lodge, see starter names when interacting, and choose only one starter.
- Make the chosen starter usable in battles against visually distinct wild creatures in tall grass.

## Decisions
- The game is an original creature-catching adventure called Wildbound.
- Starter species are Bramblehare, Cindercub, and Brooklet; Mosskin and Pufflet are additional species.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added five species with distinct colors, HP, icons, drawing variants, and two attack names each.
- Added lodge interior, starter displays, lodge navigation, and one-time starter selection with `starterChosen` persistence and legacy-save handling.
- Added distinct wild encounters using Mosskin and Pufflet and wired both attack buttons to their respective starter attacks.
- `node --check game.js` passed.
- Browser smoke test selected Cindercub and confirmed the choice was saved in `localStorage`; a Mosskin battle appeared, and Tailflare reduced its HP.
- Changed battle actions to a two-column grid and moved the battle message upward to prevent overlap.

### Active
- Fix and re-verify battle UI positioning: a desktop browser measurement still showed the battle message overlapping the first row of buttons.
- Test lodge re-entry and one-starter-only behavior, battle flow and distinct encounters, catch/save/reload behavior, and mobile layouts.

### Blocked
- (none)

1. Adjust battle message/action positioning so they do not overlap at desktop or mobile sizes; recheck all four actions fit within the battle overlay.
2. Run browser tests for starter persistence and exclusive choice, catching creatures, save/reload behavior, and distinct wild encounters.
3. Check desktop and mobile layouts, including the battle controls.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: World rendering, lodge/starter logic, species, battle logic, and save state.
- `index.html`: Battle buttons, including `#attack-two-btn`.
- `style.css`: Battle layout and responsive rules; latest positioning changes need verification.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed the game and supporting files as untracked.

- Complete Wildbound as a creature-catching game with three animal-inspired starters and battles.
- Improve Willow Lodge interactions and interior: make starter selection clear, decorate the room, and resize/block the table appropriately.

- Preserve the original pixel-art style and use original creatures and assets.
- Let players enter the lodge, see starter names when interacting, and choose only one starter.
- Ensure the chosen starter can battle visually distinct wild creatures in tall grass.
- Make the selection interaction text fully visible and provide clear selection options, or automatically choose the capsule interacted with.
- Decorate the lodge interior and adjust the table’s size and collision so it is not oversized or walk-through.

## Decisions
- The game is an original creature-catching adventure called Wildbound.
- Starter species are Bramblehare, Cindercub, and Brooklet; Mosskin and Pufflet are additional species.

- Added five species with distinct colors, HP, icons, drawing variants, and two attack names each.
- Added lodge interior and navigation, one-time starter selection with `starterChosen` persistence, and legacy-save handling.
- Added wild encounters using Mosskin and Pufflet and connected both attack buttons to starter attacks.
- Fixed battle UI spacing and verified it at desktop and mobile widths.
- Verified Mosskin catching, party and capsule persistence after reload, Pufflet encounters, battle completion, running and continuing, lodge re-entry, and exclusive starter selection.
- `node --check game.js` passes.

2. Add lodge decorations in the existing pixel-art style.
3. Test starter selection, movement around the table, and lodge re-entry.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: lodge rendering, movement/collision, interactions, starter selection, and persistence.
- `index.html`: game canvas and interaction UI.
- `style.css`: toast and responsive presentation.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed the project files as untracked.
